title: Reservation API in Express
idea: The reservation API exposes search, book and cancel as REST endpoints, with Express controllers, a service that owns the transaction, and a repository that holds the SQL.

analogy.text: A restaurant phone line. The receptionist takes the details, the manager checks the book and decides, and the booking ledger records the line.
analogy.breaks: A receptionist forgets repeat calls; the Idempotency-Key does not.

points: Controllers parse input with `zod` and map results to status codes only.
The service runs best fit and insert in one transaction, retrying 23P01 or 40P01.
A repeated Idempotency-Key returns the first reservation with 200, not a new one.
One error middleware maps validation, domain and database errors to HTTP codes.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controller and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL 18.

walk.text: Demo schema: one restaurant, a two-seat and a four-seat table, and the overlap constraint.
`tx` gives each service call one transaction and always releases the client.
Repository: seating length, key lookup, best-fit table, and the insert. SQL only.
Service: replay a known key, 404 for an unknown restaurant, 409 when no table fits.
Losing the table (23P01) or a deadlock (40P01) reruns the whole transaction, three attempts at most.
Controller: demand the key, parse the body, 201 for new and 200 for a replay.
Error middleware maps each error kind to one status and a stable error code.

pitfalls: Do not choose the table in the controller; the service owns rules and the transaction.
Scope keys per customer and reject reuse with a different body; this demo skips both.
Never return raw database errors; map them to stable codes like NO_TABLE.

quiz.q: What status does the request with key k-2 print?
quiz.why: T2 already holds k-1's 19:00 reservation and T1 seats only two. Best fit finds no table, so the service throws NO_TABLE, mapped to 409.

takeaway: Controllers validate, services decide inside a transaction, repositories hold the SQL.
